name: clear-grid-zero-word
rationale: One loop-free invocation has thread_position_in_grid.x equal to zero, takes the explicit zero-index branch, and stores aligned i32 zero over the complete poisoned four-byte read/write buffer.

name: half-prefix-sums-of-small-integers-over-a-simdgroup
rationale: One simdgroup of 32 threads takes half prefix sums of in[t] = t % 5 + 1 (simd.scan.fadd.half, DESIGN D113.3, D213): out[t] = simd_prefix_inclusive_sum, the sum of in[0..=t], and out[32 + t] = simd_prefix_exclusive_sum + 1, one plus the sum of in[0..t]. Every partial sum is an integer of at most 96, exact in half whatever the order of addition, so the class's reduction-order tolerance is never needed; the + 1 makes lane 0's empty sum read 1 whichever zero it is. Every selected byte differs from the 0xab fill. The AIR has no loop.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-ten-2x1-output

The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

name: map-a-physical-coordinate-through-a-uniform-rate-map
rationale: Metal ground truth for air.map_physical_to_screen_coordinates.v2f32.p2i8.i32 (8 case-less corpus sources) through a rasterization-rate map whose rate is a uniform 1.0: a 64x64 screen, one layer, eight horizontal and eight vertical samples of 1.0, whose physical size equals its screen size in both implementations. Buffer 0 is authored as that map (DESIGN D235): the Metal oracle compiles it with newRasterizationRateMapWithDescriptor: and binds the data copyParameterDataToBuffer:offset: writes, and a Vulkan executor binds the product's parameter data of the same map (bind::RasterizationRateMap), which the engine's decoder reads; the old engine lowers the call to the identity. Four coordinates are inside the map -- (0, 0), (1.5, 2.5), (31.25, 47.75) and (63.5, 63.5) -- spanning the origin, the far corner and two interior points whose fractions are quarters, so a decoder that rounded to texel centres or floored to integers moves three of them. Three are outside it: (64, 64) is exactly one past the far edge, (80, 7.25) is sixteen past it on one axis only, and (-3.5, 2) is negative on one axis only; Metal answers the identity there (it does to x = 95 on this map and returns 0 from x = 96, outside the case), and so does the product's decoder, which extends the first or last tile's line. The last, (8.125, 55.875), is asymmetric in both axes so a transposed mapping is visible. Every coordinate is an exact binary fraction below 128, so all sixteen output words are exact in binary32 and the comparison needs no tolerance. Replaces 2ff31356, which carried Apple's parameter bytes of the same map.

name: fast-tanh-through-all-three-of-its-regimes
rationale:
air.fast_tanh.v4f32 is 259 corpus sources and air.fast_tanh.f32 another 196 -- together the largest family this translator lowers with arithmetic of its own rather than one GLSL call. It rewrites tanh as (t - 1) / (t + 1) with t = exp2(x * 2 * log2 e), and that rewrite is the thing under test: any other spelling, including the GLSL Tanh this used to be, disagrees over most of the range below.

The first four arguments are the ordinary ones. tanh(0) is exactly zero; tanh(0.5) and tanh(5) are the correctly rounded float32 results, derived in float64 and rounded once, 0 ULP against the observation; tanh(-3.75) is 1 ULP below it and carries the sign.

The last four are the three regimes the rewrite actually has, bisected on this repository's reference GPU and reproduced bit for bit through MoltenVK. Up to 43 the answer saturates to exactly 1. From 44 to about 44.35 it collapses to exactly ZERO -- not a rounding artefact but the shape of this formula, and the single most fragile fact in the family, since a lowering that saturated properly would return 1 there. From about 44.4 up, t overflows to infinity and infinity over infinity gives NaN, which is what 44.4 pins and which GLSL Tanh would answer 1.0 for. The negative side does none of this: -100 is exactly -1, because t underflows to zero and the quotient is -1 rather than a NaN. Twenty-four arguments across these regimes were probed and Metal and MoltenVK agreed on every one, including the NaN payload.

name: linked-single-threadgroup-zero-bin
rationale: One 1x1 threadgroup dispatches one invocation. kLogBinEntries=0 makes both initialization and flush loops contain exactly one bin, kTGSizeIs256=false uses the literal one-thread group size as their stride, and source_size=1x1 bounds the image path. The exact linked callback returns float4 zero without dereferencing resources; the poisoned global bin makes the local-atomic aggregation observable byte-exactly.

name: constant-half4-zero

name: linked-single-fft-temp-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded FFT work item with unit extents and strides. The destination-temp path confines writes to the authored output allocation. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert. The authored threadgroup allocation bounds the combined-radix scratch footprint.

name: three-tap-half-maximum-folds-each-channel-from-its-own-tap
rationale: MaxFilter2HRadius1 is a three-tap horizontal maximum: it samples the source at the fragment's column and at that column plus one and plus two, and folds the three RG pairs with two nested air.fmax.v2f16 calls before writing half4(max.rg, 0, 1). The whole geometry is in the params struct, so the case picks it rather than inheriting it. filter_size is 3, so the shader's radius is 1 and a source_origin of (1.5, 0.5) makes the read coordinate 0.5 + thread_index, which the embedded sampler -- pixel coordinates, nearest, clamp to edge -- resolves to texel centres; the three taps therefore land squarely on columns x, x+1 and x+2 and never on a filter boundary. destination_size.x is 6 against a threadgroup of 4, so threads 0 and 1 run the loop twice and threads 2 and 3 once, which exercises the stride-by-threadgroup-width step on both the read coordinate and the destination pixel; transposeOutput is 0, so that step is (4, 0) and the two threadgroups fill rows 0 and 1. The twelve writes are disjoint and cover the destination exactly, so no texel's value can come from another thread. The source values are multiples of 1/16, exactly representable in half and exact under any evaluation order, and were chosen so that all three properties a wrong fold would break are observable at every one of the twelve texels: the three taps are distinct in both channels, so an off-by-one tap misses; the red and green maxima come from different taps, so a fold that broadcast one lane across both misses; and the maximum differs from the minimum, so air.fmin in place of air.fmax misses. All twelve (red, green) pairs are distinct, so no texel can be satisfied by another's answer.

name: sample-one-of-32-textures-per-thread-through-one-runtime-sampler
rationale: DESIGN D299: 64 threads in two threadgroups of 32; thread g samples element g & 31 of the 32-texture array at [[texture(0)]] at (0.5, 0.5), level 0, through the sampler bound at [[sampler(0)]] (linear min and mag filters, not mipmapped, clamp to edge, normalized), and writes the float4 to out[g] at [[buffer(0)]]. Each element is a 1x1 rgba16_float texture, which every Vulkan device filters linearly, so the sample at its centre has bilinear weights (1, 0) over one clamped texel: element k reads exactly (k, 31 - 2k, k / 4, 1), every value exact in half and none a negative zero, whose sign a filter may not keep. So out[g] = (k, 31 - 2k, k / 4, 1) with k = g & 31, each of the 32 elements read twice. Where the profile has fewer than 32 samplers per stage the translator samples 32 separate textures through one separate sampler the binder writes with this bound sampler; this case is that form's observation. The observation is the whole output buffer, initially 0xab. The AIR has no loop.

name: floor-a-bilinear-quad-average-into-an-unsigned-yuv-texel
rationale: The kernel's constexpr sampler is `coord::pixel` with a linear min and mag filter, so every tap lands at an integer pixel coordinate and the filter weight is exactly one half on both axes: each sample is the exact average of a two-by-two texel quad. Every texel channel is a multiple of a quarter, so those averages are multiples of a sixteenth and are exact in binary16 and in binary32 alike, and the whole result is fixed before any rounding mode can matter. `_regions[4]` and `_regions[5]` are 0.75 and 0.5: `air.convert.u.i16.f.f32` truncates both to a zero origin, so the sample base is `2*gid` -- had it rounded to nearest, 0.75 would have become an origin of one, every base would have shifted by two texels and all sixteen output texels would differ. The first four floats of the buffer are 11.5, -2.25, 99.0 and 0.5, which the reflected footprint says are never read; if a decoder walked the buffer from its start instead of from byte 16 it would pick one of them up and the origin would not be zero. Each thread takes five taps at base + (-1,1), (3,1), (1,-1), (1,3) and (1,1), converts each through the same BT.709 matrix, and writes floor(255 * (Y, Cb, Cr)) of the centre tap into the first three channels of a `texture2d<ushort, write>`. gid.x = 0 and gid.y = 0 place taps at pixel coordinate -1, whose two contributing texels both clamp to index 0, and the eight-wide texture puts gid = 3's outer taps at coordinate 9, which clamps to index 7 -- so both edges of `clamp_to_edge` are exercised. The alpha channel is the largest component of |yuv(x+3) - yuv(x-1)| + |yuv(y+3) - yuv(y-1)|, clamped to one: three of the sixteen threads exceed one and land on 255 through `air.fast_fmin`, and across the grid the largest component is Y in some threads, Cb in others and Cr in others, so a fixed-channel maximum would be visible. Every pre-floor product sits at least 0.12 away from an integer, which is three orders of magnitude past the worst binary32 error the dot products can accumulate, so the floor absorbs association but not a wrong lowering.

name: widen-a-wrapped-sample-origin-without-a-sign
rationale: Same kernel, but the sample origin is chosen so that the two unsigned conversions have to be unsigned. `_regions[4]` is 1.75 and `_regions[5]` is 40000.75, and `air.convert.u.i16.f.f32` truncates them to 1 and 40000. 40000 does not fit in a signed short: a signed conversion would have clamped it to 32767, and the resulting base would have differed by 14466 texels, which lands on a different clamp only because it stays past the edge -- so the assertion that carries the signedness is the shift, not the clamp. The kernel subtracts the origin in 16-bit lanes and shifts left by one before widening, so gid.y = 0 gives (0 - 40000) mod 65536 = 25536, doubled to 51072, and `air.convert.f.v2f32.u.v2i16` must widen that as 51072.0 rather than as -14464.0. Every y tap therefore clamps to texture row 7 and all four output rows are identical; a signed widening would have given -14464, whose taps clamp to row 0 instead, and rows 0 and 7 of this texture do not agree. On x the origin is 1, so gid.x = 0 wraps to 65534 and clamps to the right edge while gid.x = 1, 2 and 3 sample the first three quads normally: the first output column differs from the other three and the wrap is visible without leaving the same dispatch. Alpha is zero in the wrapped column, where the two x taps land on the same clamped quad and the difference is exactly zero, and non-zero in the rest.

name: half-sin-cos-tan-and-sincos-of-the-infinities-under-fast-math
rationale: Thread i reads the half pattern in[i] as x, one of +0, -0, +inf and -inf (0x0000, 0x8000, 0x7c00, 0xfc00), and writes one uint4: sin(x) | cos(x) << 16, tan(x) | s << 16, c, and the pattern of x, where s = sincos(x, c). The zeros anchor the finite answers: cos of a zero is 1, and sin, tan and sincos's sine of a zero are a zero, whose sign the case records. Compiled with the default fast math: the half calls carry LLVM's fast flags, under which an infinite operand is undefined (MSL section 7.1). Question (WP-MLO, TODO 2.8, DESIGN D324 item 2): does Metal answer them as it does without fast math (WP-UNV's probe UNV-metal-probe-1 read 0x7e00 in both modes), so that one answer serves both.

name: dsm-b-matrix-multiply-add-on-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-after-a-whole-load
rationale: DESIGN D271 (b), D159.9(d): lanes 0-15 of one simdgroup of 32 run the multiply-add on fragments all 32 lanes loaded (simdgroup_load, convergent) before the branch; lanes 16-31 are inactive for it. Metal leaves it undefined. Lanes 0-15 hold rows 0-3, so their results read b rows 4-7 from the inactive lanes: b[(r + 4) & 7][j] + c[r][j] if the hardware reads the inactive lanes' loaded registers, c[r][j] if it reads zero. Inputs (A): a is the row rotation a[r][(r + 4) & 7] = 1 (else 0), b[k][j] = 8k + j + 1, c[r][j] = 256 + 8r + j, so a whole simdgroup's d[r][j] = b[(r + 4) & 7][j] + c[r][j]: each result row is the b row four rows away, which another half of the simdgroup holds. Every cell, product, and sum is an integer below 2048, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop.

name: dsm-b-matrix-multiply-add-on-lanes-zero-to-fifteen-after-a-whole-load-other-inputs

Inputs (B): a is the row rotation with a[r][(r + 4) & 7] = 2 where that column is 0, 1, 4, or 5 (the even lanes' columns) and 1 elsewhere, b[k][j] = 8k + j + 1 plus 64 in rows 4-7 (the cells lanes 16-31 hold), c[r][j] = 256 + 8r + j: input A with the even lanes' a cells and lanes 16-31's b cells changed. Every cell, product, and sum is an integer below 2048, exact in float and half whatever the accumulation order. out[2g + j] is lane g's float cell j, out[2n + 2g + j] its half cell widened (n the grid's threads); a lane that does not run the multiply-add leaves its words at the 0xAB poison. The AIR has no loop.

name: small-transcendental-leftovers
rationale: Six air.* symbols the corpus reaches only once or twice each and that no authored case covered: air.fast_sinh.f32, air.fast_cosh.f32, air.round.f32, air.sqrt.v2f16, air.cos.v2f16 and air.sinpi.f16. They share one kernel because none is worth a fixture alone and their arguments do not interact. air.round.f32 is the one with a claim behind it: Metal's round breaks a .5 tie AWAY FROM ZERO, which GLSL.std.450 Round explicitly leaves to the implementation, so the lowering picks RoundEven's opposite deliberately and until now nothing pinned it -- the four tie rows 0.5, -0.5, 2.5, -2.5 answer 1, -1, 3, -3 where RoundEven would answer 0, -0, 2, -2. The half rows are asked where the answer is exact, because a half transcendental is not reliably byte-authorable through MoltenVK: sqrt at the perfect squares, sinpi at the half-integers where the reduction residue is 0. The second cos lane, cos(half(1)), is the one deliberate inexact row, present to find out whether a half cosine agrees when only Tanh and Atan2 were known to split by width; it does, both answering 0x3853. sinh and cosh are fast:: at both widths in SPIRV-Cross and the AIR names air.fast_*, so they agree by construction and take an ordinary argument. Every argument is read from a buffer so nothing folds, and results are bit-cast into one uint buffer so a single output region carries both widths without a conversion that would round.
